case_name: Govindrao Ranoji Musale vs Sou. Anandibai And Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: Sou. Anandibai And Anr. (wife and another party)

facts_of_case: Appellant, a Hindu man, was married to respondent No. 2 in 1934. He then married respondent No. 1 in 1959 while still married to respondent No. 2. Respondent No. 1 lived with her parents for five years after being driven away by the appellant and later filed a suit for maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: A codifying Act provides the law for a particular branch of law.
legal_principles.held: It is well settled that the object of codification of a particular branch of law is that on any matter specifically dealt with by it, the law should be sought for in the codifying enactment itself.

legal_principles.principle: A provision in a statute that confers a remedy also creates a corresponding right.
legal_principles.held: This power conferred upon the Court clearly creates a corresponding right in the wife or the husband to get maintenance provided the conditions laid down for the grant of the same are satisfied.

legal_principles.principle: A court should not normally construe a provision in a statute to make it redundant.
legal_principles.held: Hence, if the submission of Mr. Pendse is accepted, it would mean that the provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, in so far as they deal with the claim of the husband for maintenance, would be redundant; and such a construction should not normally be resorted to.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decision was upheld, and respondent No. 1 was entitled to maintenance from the appellant.
